title: Componentized streaming and action contracts — PRD (draft)
body:
Summary:
This doc outlines a componentized PRD for: 1) streaming response primitives, 2) a lightweight action/tool-calling contract, and 3) structured output shapes that are ergonomic for client libraries. The goal is a small, composable surface that teams can adopt incrementally — streaming-only, actions-only, or both.

Context / why now:
- Increasing customer demand for low-latency UI streaming (token-level events) while still supporting reliable tool invocations and typed outputs for product features (e.g., receipts, invoices, forms).
- Existing hosted-api sketches have overlapping ideas; this tries to separate concerns into clear contracts so SDKs, runtimes, and rollouts can be developed in parallel.

Goals:
- Deliver a minimal streaming wire protocol that supports partial-text tokens, structured deltas, and event markers (start/patch/complete/error).
- Define an actions contract where model can request a named action with typed args and receive typed responses; actions must be routable to 3rd-party connectors or builtin tools.
- Standardize a structured-output envelope so SDKs can materialize typed objects without brittle parsing heuristics.
- Keep ergonomics simple for client SDKs: streaming consumer API should be a small iterator/async callback; actions should map to a promise-based handler with automatic fallback.

Non-goals:
- Not introducing new heavyweight model-side control tokens or changes to model training. This is strictly inference-time protocol/SDK surface work.
- Not building connectors for every partner; connectors are a separate roadmap item.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Wire-level streaming primitives
- Events: {"type":"partial","payload":"..."} | {"type":"delta","path":"form.items[0]","value":...} | {"type":"action_request","name":"search_docs","args":{"q":"..."}} | {"type":"action_result","id":"123","result":{}} | {"type":"done"} | {"type":"error","message":"..."}
- Transport: HTTP streaming (chunked) + SSE as fallback. Each chunk is newline-delimited JSON event. Backward-compatible: non-streaming response remains final JSON blob.

2) Action/tool calling contract
- Model emits action_request event with: id, name, args_schema-name (optional), and optional input_surfaces (text fragments).
- Server publishes action_request into a routing layer (policy: by name, customer whitelist, region). SDK exposes a handler registration: registerActionHandler(name, async (args, meta) => result).
- Timeouts and fallbacks: action_request includes suggested_timeout_ms; if no handler returns in time, runtime emits action_timeout event and model can be resumed with fallback tokens.
- Security: action names must be whitelisted at customer level for Private/Dedicated tenants.

3) Structured output envelope
- Final outputs should include an explicit schema reference string (e.g., "schema://redwood/v1/form-v1") and a top-level typed payload: {"schema_ref":"...","data":{...}}.
- Intermediate deltas may reference paths into the data object to allow progressive hydration in the client UI.

SDK ergonomics notes (guiding principles):
- Keep streaming API minimal: onMessage callback or async iterator; developer should be able to transform events into partial UI updates without parsing raw text.
- Tool handler pattern: registerActionHandler('name', async (args, context) => ({status:'ok', result})) returns a promise. SDK returns an action_result event back into the stream when resolved.
- Retry/fallback helpers: SDK should expose simple helpers: callWithFallbacks(request, [{model:'x'}, {model:'y'}]) that orchestrate model-level fallback.
- Typed bindings: generate TypeScript bindings from schema_ref for common shapes to minimize ad-hoc parsing.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experimental): implement streaming wire + local action handler in hosted dev cluster; opt-in flag for customers. (1 quarter)
- Phase 1 (beta): whitelist-based action routing, schema_ref enforcement for structured outputs, SDK alpha (js/ts + python). (2 quarters)
- Phase 2 (GA): SLA+analytics, server-side connectors, admin UI for action whitelists and schema catalog. (ongoing)

Metrics / success criteria:
- Adoption: number of active hosts using streaming >= 50 within 3 months of beta
- Latency: median time-to-first-token <= 70ms for 95th pct of streaming requests in hosted regions
- Reliability: action round-trip success rate >= 99% in beta for internal connectors
- Developer ergonomics: >80% of pilot SDK users rate ergonomics 4/5+ in survey

Risks / open questions:
- Compatibility with models that emit freeform instructions vs structured action requests — need a guardrail or model-observed patterns.
- Edge case: interleaving of multiple simultaneous action_requests from same session — how to order and resume context correctly.
- Billing implications: partial streaming vs final tokens accounting — confirm with finance.

Unresolved implementation notes / TODOs:
- Define exact event JSON envelope (fields, mandatory/optional). (action: Priya)
- Run perf microbench for chunked HTTP streaming vs SSE vs websocket for our infra. (action: Ethan)
- Draft TypeScript codegen for schema_ref => interfaces and client helpers. (action: Miguel)
- Security review for cross-tenant action routing and HSM/KMS considerations. (action: Riley)

Appendix / sketches:
- Example JS streaming consumer:
  const stream = client.stream({model:'rwd-stream-1', prompt:'...'});
  for await (const evt of stream) {
    if (evt.type === 'partial') renderText(evt.payload);
    if (evt.type === 'delta') applyPatch(evt.path, evt.value);
    if (evt.type === 'action_request') {
      // optional local handler
      const res = await handlers.handle(evt.name, evt.args);
      stream.sendActionResult(evt.id, res);
    }
  }
Next steps:
- Sync with serving-runtime and infra teams next Tue (link in linked_artifacts) to align on transport choices.
- Create initial PRD ticket JIRA-API-3301 with the event envelope draft attached.
- Schedule SDK pairing week with developer-experience to prototype lightweight handlers.

Notes to self: keep the contracts incremental. If we try to do everything in one pass we will block GA. Focus on clean event envelope and action handler flow first.
